cities.base: La Candelaria or nearby, for walking distance to Plaza Bolívar, Museo del Oro and Museo Botero
cities.name: Bogotá

cities.base: El Poblado, for the restaurants and a safe, easy base for Comuna 13 and Metrocable day trips
cities.name: Medellín

cities.base: day trip from El Poblado, Medellín
cities.name: Guatape and El Peñol

cities.base: day trip from El Poblado, Medellín via Metrocable
cities.name: Parque Arvi

places.name: La Candelaria street walk (Calle del Embudo area)
places.note: Narrow colonial streets, street art, small cafes. Skip paying for a guided walking tour, the plazas and murals carry it themselves.

places.name: Museo Botero
places.note: Boteros plus his own collection, with some Picasso and Monet; free, closed Tuesday, open 09:00 to 19:00 and 10:00 to 17:00 on Sunday. An hour and a half covers it.

places.name: Monserrate
places.note: Funicular up in the morning, cable car from noon, footpath from 05:00 but shut Tuesday; a 2022 listing had 23,500 pesos return, 14,000 on Sunday, so hours vary, check. Go early, cloud kills the view by early afternoon.

places.name: Museo del Oro
places.note: The best museum in the country, worth building the day around; closed Monday, 09:00 to 18:00 and 10:00 to 16:00 on Sunday, when it is free. Entry was 5,000 pesos on a 2021 city list, which also gave 17:00, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Plaza de Bolívar
places.note: Cathedral, Capitolio and Palacio Liévano ring the square. Pigeons and vendors, worth a slow loop but don't linger past 30-40 minutes.

places.name: Museo Nacional
places.note: A fallback for the last afternoon if La Candelaria is done; 09:00 to 17:00, closed Monday, 3,000 pesos in 2021 and the 2025 tariff may have raised it, check the price. Free Wednesday 15:00 to 17:00.

places.name: Santo Domingo Metrocable
places.note: The ride up is the experience more than anything at the top; Line K runs 04:30 to 23:00, 08:30 to 22:00 on Sunday, on the normal metro fare of about 3,100 to 3,500 pesos in June 2026.

places.name: El Poblado
places.note: Not a sight, just where you eat well and sit outside for one or two evenings.

places.name: Comuna 13
places.note: Go with a local guide, not solo; the graffiti and escalators tell the transformation story better than any museum.

places.name: Zona G
places.note: Bogotá's dinner neighborhood, not a sight.

places.name: Plaza Bolívar
places.note: The anchor of La Candelaria's walk; the streets around it carry the history without needing a guide.

places.name: Cafe con vista at La Piedra summit
places.note: Small snack bar built right at the top of the rock, basic coffee and drinks with the reservoir view as the backdrop. Convenient rather than good, but you're already up there.

places.name: Zipline attractions near La Piedra
places.note: Short, overpriced ziplines set up for tour groups near the rock's parking area. Fun for five minutes but not worth cutting into your limited day here.

places.name: Stalls at the base of La Piedra
places.note: Vendors selling snacks, drinks and souvenirs at the rock's base. Fine for a cold coconut water after the climb, nothing you need to seek out otherwise.

places.name: Mirador Antiguo Peñol
places.note: Marks the site of the original town of El Peñol, flooded in the 1970s for the hydroelectric project. A short stop with some historical weight, easy to combine with the rock since it's on the way.

places.name: Embalse boat tour
places.note: Short boat rides on the reservoir depart from the malecon, passing the flooded old town of El Peñol submerged when the dam was built. Worth it if you have spare time after lunch, skippable if you're tight on the return drive.

places.name: El Rancherito de Guatape
places.note: Solid trout lunch spot near the waterfront, typical Antioquia plates. Nothing fancy, reliable after the rock climb.

places.name: Parque Principal de Guatape
places.note: Central square with the church and the town's best concentration of zocalo houses around it. Good starting point to orient yourself before wandering.

places.name: Calle de los Zocalos
places.note: The colorful zocalos, the painted relief panels on the base of every house, are the actual visual identity of the town, more than the rock. Walk a few blocks off the main square to see the older, less-restored ones.

places.name: Artisan shops on Calle Sucre
places.note: Handicrafts, hammocks, and the usual magnet and keychain souvenirs. Decent for a last stop before heading back to the van or car for Medellin.

places.name: Guided tuk-tuk town tour
places.note: Tuk-tuk drivers offer quick loops around town narrating the zocalos. The town is small enough and flat enough to walk yourself in the same time, skip unless you're short on energy after the rock.

places.name: Metrocable Line K to Santo Domingo
places.note: Part of the regular metro, not a tourist ride, over the Comuna 1 and 2 rooftops; Line K runs 04:30 to 23:00, Sunday 08:30 to 22:00, and stops at Santo Domingo, where Line L to Arvi starts.

places.name: Metrocable Line L (Santo Domingo to Arvi)
places.note: Separate ticket, about 6,500 to 8,000 pesos one way in 2026, over pine forest; 09:00 to 18:00, from 08:30 Sunday. It shuts in high wind, and the Metro lists it closed Monday, so check.

places.name: Parque Arvi main ecological park entrance
places.note: Entry is free; the arrival plaza where trails, market and food stalls start, crowded at weekends. Hiking 10:00 to 16:30, closed Tuesday per a May 2025 city notice, and Line L may not run Monday, so check.

places.name: Mercado Verde de Arvi (farmers market)
places.note: Runs Friday through Sunday only, small stalls selling arepas, fruit, honey and plants from surrounding vereda farms, worth timing your visit around if you want lunch here.

places.name: Sendero Camino de Piedras
places.note: A signed forest path on an old stone route once used by indigenous traders, flat, shaded and quiet; park hiking runs 10:00 to 16:30, closed Tuesday per a May 2025 city notice, so check.

places.name: Sendero Piedras Marcadas (petroglyphs)
places.note: Requires a park guide to access, leads to pre-Columbian rock carvings, genuinely interesting if you have the extra hour, skippable if you're only doing the half day trip from Santo Domingo.

places.name: Laguna Esmeralda
places.note: Small forest lagoon a short walk past the main plaza, a quiet stop rather than a destination, easy to combine with the stone path.

places.name: Mirador de las Torres
places.note: A clearing with a view back down toward the Aburra valley, worth the short detour on a clear morning, often clouded over by early afternoon.

places.name: Parque Lineal La Piedra (stream walk near Santo Domingo)
places.note: A small neighborhood creek-side walk right by the Santo Domingo cable station, useful if you have a few minutes before or after the ride and want to see the barrio at ground level rather than only from the cabin.

places.name: Guided birdwatching and nature interpretation walks
places.note: Skip unless you're genuinely into birdwatching, these run long, need advance booking through the park office, and eat the half day you have budgeted for Arvi on this itinerary.

places.name: Hacienda restaurant stalls near the plaza (comida tipica)
places.note: Simple sit-down spots by the main plaza serving trout, arepas and aguapanela, nothing fancy, but reasonable and convenient if you don't want to carry lunch back down on the cable car.

places.name: Malecon de Guatape
places.note: Boardwalk along the reservoir with the tourist boats lined up. Pleasant enough for a stroll after lunch but don't build the day around it.

places.name: La Piedra del Peñol
places.note: 740 steps built into a crack in the rock, no technical climbing, just stairs and crowds. Go early, before 10am, or the queue on the stairs itself slows you down. The view of the reservoir's finger-like inlets is the reason to come and it delivers.

places.name: Parque Berrío
places.note: Skip lingering here, it's the old central plaza but it's mostly transit chaos and street vendors now, better as a walk-through on the way to Plaza Botero than a stop of its own.

places.name: Museo Casa de la Memoria
places.note: Free museum on the armed conflict and the city's violent decades, heavy but well done; closed Monday, 09:00 to 18:00 Tuesday to Friday, 10:00 to 16:00 at weekends. A counterweight if Comuna 13 felt too polished.

places.name: Feria de San Alejo
places.note: Antiques and crafts market that only runs the first Saturday of the month in Parque Bolívar. Only worth building a morning around if the date happens to line up with your trip.

places.name: Parque Explora
places.note: Interactive science museum and aquarium by the botanical garden, built for families more than solo travellers; closed Monday, 08:30 to 16:00 weekdays, 10:00 to 17:00 weekends, check the price. A rainy-day backup.

places.name: Plaza Botero and Museo de Antioquia
places.note: 23 Botero bronzes outdoors in a plaza rough at the edges, so watch your bag; the museum behind adds Botero paintings and colonial work, 09:40 to 17:30, 16:30 Sunday, and an older list had 22,000 pesos for foreigners, check the price.

places.name: Metrocable to Parque Arvi (Santo Domingo line)
places.note: Over Comuna 1 and 2 rooftops into pine forest at 2,400m; Line L runs 09:00 to 18:00, about 6,500 to 8,000 pesos one way. The Metro says closed Monday but the city says the park opens Mondays, so check.

places.name: Guatapé waterfront town
places.note: Painted zocalo relief panels on nearly every building, lakeside malecón for lunch. Gets crowded with day-trippers off tour buses, it's still worth the walk.

places.name: El Peñol Rock (La Piedra del Peñol)
places.note: 649 steps built into a crack in the granite monolith. Line for the stairs backs up midday, go early. View at the top over the reservoir is the reason to do the whole day trip.

places.name: Comuna 13 San Javier
places.note: Outdoor escalators and graffiti murals built over what was one of the most violent barrios in the city. Go with a local guide for the context, not just the photos, and go in the afternoon when vendors and dancers are actually out.

places.name: La Puerta Falsa
places.note: Tiny, centuries-old spot for tamales and ajiaco and chocolate santafereño. Good cheap lunch stop between Plaza Bolívar and Museo del Oro.

places.name: Andrés Carne de Res (Andrés DC branch)
places.note: Loud, theatrical, touristy grill and nightlife spot. Fun once if you want a big night out, skippable if you'd rather have a quiet dinner.

places.name: Chorro de Quevedo
places.note: Small plaza said to be the founding site of the city, students and buskers around it. Worth a five minute stop while walking La Candelaria, not a destination on its own.

places.name: Usaquén Sunday Market
places.note: Sundays only, 09:00 to 18:00 on a 2022 city listing, at Calle 119 with Carrera 6A: crafts, antiques and food stalls in a plaza far from the centre. Only fits if your last day lands on a Sunday.

places.name: Catedral de Sal (Zipaquirá)
places.note: Skip on this itinerary, it's an hour outside Bogotá and eats a half day you don't have across only 3 nights in the city.

places.name: Museo Nacional de Colombia
places.note: National history and art in a former prison, less crowded than Museo del Oro; 09:00 to 17:00, closed Monday, 3,000 pesos in 2021, check the price. Free Wednesday 15:00 to 17:00, and some Sundays, check.

places.name: Restaurante La Matriarca
places.note: A paisa classic in Poblado: order the bandeja paisa, 59,000 pesos in the El Colombiano survey of 9 October 2026, or the ceviche. Open to 22:00 or later Monday to Saturday but only to 17:30 on Sunday.

places.name: Mondongo's El Poblado
places.note: The long-running paisa chain: mondongo soup or the bandeja paisa, 61,500 pesos in the El Colombiano survey of 9 October 2026. Open 11:30 to 21:00, Sunday 11:00 to 20:00.

places.name: Mondongo's La 70
places.note: The Laureles branch, a more local crowd near La 70's bars; the bandeja paisa at 61,500 pesos is the chain's menu price in the El Colombiano survey of 9 October 2026, not this branch's menu. Open 11:30 to 21:00, Sunday to 20:00.

places.name: Hatoviejo Centro
places.note: The lunch stop on the Plaza Botero morning, walkable from the museum, open 08:00 to 19:00 daily; the Hato Viejo bandeja paisa at 66,500 pesos is the chain's menu price in the El Colombiano survey of 9 October 2026.

places.name: Hatoviejo Buenos Aires
places.note: Grill, brunch and an espresso bar beside the paisa menu; the bandeja paisa at 66,500 pesos is the chain's menu price in the El Colombiano survey of 9 October 2026. Open from 09:00 to 23:00 most nights, to 21:00 Sunday.

places.name: El Castillo Museum and Gardens
places.note: A 1930 French-style castle with gardens, seen on a guided visit; open daily, 09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays and from 10:00 at weekends. Listed at 8.60 with no currency named, so check the price.

places.name: Casa Museo Pedro Nel Gómez
places.note: The house and murals of the muralist and architect, 09:00 to 17:00, closed Sunday. One listing gives a fee and a visitor says it is free, so check the price.

places.name: Palacio de la Cultura Rafael Uribe Uribe
places.note: The Belgian-designed landmark with the striped facade in Centro, free, bring photo ID; 08:00 to 17:00 on weekdays but only to 14:00 Saturday, closed Sunday.

places.name: Jardín Botánico de Medellín
places.note: Free, next door to Parque Explora, and the butterfly house is a separate ticket, check the price. Closed Monday, 09:30 to 16:00, from 09:00 at weekends.

places.name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM)
places.note: The modern art museum in Ciudad del Río, closed Monday, 11:00 to 19:00 Tuesday to Friday and to 18:00 at weekends. Foreigners pay more than residents and the listing names no currency, so check the price.

places.name: Cementerio Museo San Pedro
places.note: A 19th-century cemetery that is also a museum, open 08:00 to 17:00 daily; no day price was listed, so check the price, and there is a paid guided night tour.

places.name: Cerro Nutibara (Parque de Esculturas)
places.note: The hill in the middle of the city with a sculpture park and the Pueblito Paisa replica village on top; free, 08:00 to 22:00 daily.

places.name: Museo Universidad de Antioquia
places.note: The university's museum, free, but you register at the campus gate; 08:00 to 17:00 Tuesday to Friday, only 09:00 to 13:00 Saturday, closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Casa Gardeliana
places.note: A small free house museum to Carlos Gardel in Manrique, 10:00 to 17:00, closed Sunday; 45 minutes is plenty.

places.name: Casa Museo Otraparte
places.note: A heritage house museum down in Envigado, 11:00 to 18:30, closed Sunday; no price was listed, so check the price.

places.name: Parroquia Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria
places.note: The Candelaria parish church in Centro, a short stop on a walk through the centre; no hours or price were listed, so hours vary, check, and check the price for any paid area.

outings.why: Plaza Bolívar and the narrow colonial streets carry themselves; skip the paid guided tour unless you want the history spelled out.
outings.name: La Candelaria walking

outings.why: Cable car or funicular up, walk down or vice versa; go early because the view is the whole point and fog ruins it by afternoon.
outings.name: Monserrate cerro
outings.fallback: Museo Botero or a second museum if cloud cover kills the view.

outings.why: Go with a local guide, not solo, and go in the afternoon when the community events and vendors are out.
outings.name: Comuna 13 graffiti tour and escalators

outings.why: Climb the rock, walk the waterfront town, lunch there; 2 hours each way plus 3-4 hours on site, don't try to add anything else to this day.
outings.name: El Peñol rock and Guatape waterfront

outings.why: Cable car into the park and back down by early afternoon; skip the guided nature walks inside unless you're genuinely into birdwatching, the ride up is the experience.
outings.name: Metrocable to Santo Domingo and Parque Arvi

destination.name: Colombia (Bogotá + Medellín)
destination.pitch: Two cities in a week, not three: Bogotá's altitude and gold, Medellín's transformation story and Guatape, Cartagena sacrificed for time.
destination.caveat: The internal flight eats half a travel day each way and six nights across two cities means you never settle into either one. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Bogotá's La Candelaria and Medellín's Comuna 13 both work as walkable urban days with a real story behind them.
because.nature: Guatape's rock and Parque Arvi's cable car give you mountain air without needing extra days for it.
because.culture: Museo del Oro is the best museum in the country and Comuna 13 tells the transformation story better than any brochure.
because.exploration: Comuna 13's escalators and Metrocable up to Santo Domingo are as much transit as sightseeing.
